questions.question: In CSDM 5, what was the Service Instance table (cmdb_ci_service_auto) previously labeled as?

options.text: Business Service
Application Service
Technology Service
Technical Service

explanation.correct: The cmdb_ci_service_auto table was previously labeled Application Service. In CSDM 5, it was relabeled to Service Instance because there are now multiple types of service instances (Application Service, Data Service Instance, Network Service Instance, etc.), not just application services. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/csdm-service-instance.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Business Service is a separate table in the Service Consumption domain that represents the business functions that depend on technology.
Technology Service was relabeled to Technology Management Service in CSDM 5 and is used to identify groups responsible for providing technology.
Technical Service is not a standard CSDM label. The correct previous label was Application Service.

source.excerpt: Service Instance. This is a preexisting table inside of ServiceNow. This is the cmdb_ci_service_auto table. Previously, this was labeled Application Service.

questions.question: Which new Service Instance types were added in CSDM 5 in addition to Application Service? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Data Service Instance
Network Service Instance
Business Service Instance
Facility Service Instance

explanation.correct: CSDM 5 added five new service instance types beyond Application Service: Data Service Instance, Network Service Instance, Connection Service Instance, Facility Service Instance, and Operational Process Service Instance. Business Service Instance is not one of the new types - Business Service remains a separate concept in the Service Consumption domain. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/csdm-service-instance-types.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Business Service is not a Service Instance type. Business Service exists in the Service Consumption domain and represents business functions that consume technology.

source.excerpt: We added five more service instances... we have a Data Service Instance. We've got a Network Service Instance, Connection Service Instance, Facility Service Instance, and then an Operational Process Service Instance.

questions.question: What is a Dynamic CI Group and why is it valuable in the Service Delivery domain?

options.text: A group of users who can modify CI records dynamically
A programmatic way to group CIs based on criteria rather than manual relationships
A temporary grouping of CIs during maintenance windows
A dashboard widget that displays CI counts dynamically

explanation.correct: Dynamic CI Group uses various methods to programmatically group CIs together based on criteria, eliminating the need to manually relate CIs into collections. This enables capabilities like managing manual metadata and grouping CIs for patch management. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/dynamic-ci-groups.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dynamic CI Group is about grouping CIs, not managing user permissions. User groups are handled separately in the platform.
Dynamic CI Groups are persistent groupings based on criteria, not temporary maintenance groupings.
Dynamic CI Group is a CI class in the CMDB, not a dashboard widget. It's used to logically group CIs.

source.excerpt: Dynamic CI Group... uses various methods to group CIs together so that you can programmatically identify CIs, as opposed to manually relating CIs into a collection or into a group.

questions.question: An organization needs to track four different portfolio types: technology services, business capabilities, product delivery, and customer-facing products. According to CSDM, how should these portfolios be structured?

options.text: All four should use the same portfolio structure based on departments
Technology Management Services by shared IT services, Business Services by capabilities, Service Instances by value streams, and Products by product lines
Create custom portfolio tables for each type
Use only the Service Catalog to organize all portfolio types

explanation.correct: CSDM recommends different portfolio structures for different purposes: Technology Management Services organized by shared IT services, Business Services organized by business capability structure, Service Instances organized across product/value streams for manufacturing and delivery, and products sold externally organized by product lines. See: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/zurich-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/concept/csdm-portfolios.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Different portfolio types serve different personas and purposes, requiring different organizational structures.
CSDM provides guidance using out-of-box tables and structures. Creating custom tables increases technical debt.
Service Catalog is for service requests, not portfolio management. Different portfolio views serve different strategic purposes.

source.excerpt: Technology management services, shared IT services are an easy way to think about how to maybe structure those portfolio constructs. Business services, they're often managed through a business capability structure... Service instances are really how we actually think about the manufacturing and delivery... oriented across product streams.

questions.question: What role is required to create a CMDB Data Manager policy in CMDB Workspace?

options.text: itil
sn_cmdb_admin
cmdb_user
data_manager_user

explanation.correct: The sn_cmdb_admin role is explicitly required to create CMDB Data Manager policies in CMDB Workspace, as stated in the ServiceNow documentation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The itil role provides access to ITSM modules but does not grant permission to create Data Manager policies.
The cmdb_user role provides basic CMDB read access but lacks the administrative privileges needed to create Data Manager policies.
The data_manager_user role is used for assigning policy tasks to specific users, not for creating the policies themselves.

source.excerpt: Role required: sn_cmdb_admin

questions.question: What happens when an administrator tries to create a CMDB Data Manager policy of type Retire, Archive, or Delete without an active retirement definition for the targeted class?

options.text: The policy is created but remains in a Draft state until the retirement definition is added
An error message appears and the operation fails
The policy is created successfully but the CIs are excluded during task execution
The system automatically generates a default retirement definition for the class

explanation.correct: The lifecycle policies Retire, Archive, and Delete require that an active retirement definition exists for each targeted class. If you attempt to create such a policy without this prerequisite, an error message appears and the operation fails.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The policy does not enter a Draft state — the creation operation fails immediately with an error message.
The policy cannot be created at all without the retirement definition; it is not a runtime exclusion.
ServiceNow does not auto-generate retirement definitions. Administrators must create them manually before creating lifecycle policies.

source.excerpt: The life-cycle policies Retire, Archive, and Delete, require that an active retirement definition exists for each targeted class in the policy. If you attempt to create a policy of a policy type for which this requirement applies but isn't met, an error message appears and the operation fails.

questions.question: An administrator creates a CMDB Data Manager attestation policy that targets 30,000 CIs. How will CMDB Data Manager handle the task creation?

options.text: It creates a single task containing all 30,000 CIs
It creates 3 tasks, each targeting 10,000 CIs
It fails with an error because the maximum CI limit is exceeded
It creates 30 tasks, each targeting 1,000 CIs

explanation.correct: CMDB Data Manager limits the number of target CIs per task to 10,000. When a task exceeds that number, Data Manager automatically creates as many additional tasks as needed. For 30,000 CIs, it creates 3 tasks of 10,000 CIs each.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A single task cannot exceed 10,000 CIs. Data Manager automatically splits tasks that exceed this limit.
The policy does not fail — Data Manager automatically creates additional tasks to accommodate all CIs.
The task limit is 10,000 CIs per task, not 1,000. Data Manager creates the minimum number of tasks needed.

source.excerpt: CMDB Data Manager limits the number of target CIs per task to 10,000. Therefore, when a task exceeds that number, Data Manager automatically creates as many additional tasks as needed to include all the CIs for the task. For example, if you target 30,000 CIs in an attestation task, Data Manager breaks down that task into three tasks, each targeting 10,000 CIs.

questions.question: What is the navigation path to access scripted audits in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > CMDB > Audits > Scripted Audits
All > Compliance > Scripted Audits > Audits
All > Configuration > CMDB Audits > Scripted
All > CMDB Workspace > Management > Scripted Audits

explanation.correct: The correct navigation path for scripted audits is All > Compliance > Scripted Audits > Audits. An audit type of 'Scripted' automatically filters the list.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Scripted audits are accessed through the Compliance module, not directly through the CMDB module.
There is no Configuration > CMDB Audits path. Scripted audits are under Compliance > Scripted Audits.
CMDB Workspace contains the Data Manager, not the scripted audits module. Scripted audits are accessed through the Compliance module.

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Compliance > Scripted Audits > Audits. An audit type of Scripted filters the list.

questions.question: Which field is required for a scripted audit but hidden for all other audit types?

options.text: Template
Filter
Run this script
Table

explanation.correct: The Filter field is required for scripted audits but is hidden for all other audit types. It defines the records the scripted audit evaluates.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Template field works in the opposite way — it is required for other audit types but is hidden when the audit type is Scripted.
The 'Run this script' field appears only when you access audits from the Scripted Audits module, but it is not described as hidden for other types in the same way Filter is.
The Table field is read-only and displays the table for the template. It is not specific to scripted audits as a required field.

source.excerpt: Filter: Filter to use when the audit type is Scripted. This field is required for scripted audits, but is hidden for all other audit types.

questions.question: An administrator is configuring a CMDB Data Manager policy and selects 'User Field' as the Assignment type. Which table do the columns listed in the Task assignment dropdown reference?

options.text: Group [sys_user_group]
User [sys_user]
Task [task]
Configuration Item [cmdb_ci]

explanation.correct: When the Assignment type is 'User Field', the Task assignment dropdown is dynamically populated with columns in the policy's table that reference the User [sys_user] table, such as 'Attested by' and 'Assigned to'. Records are grouped by this column and tasks are assigned to the resulting users.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Group [sys_user_group] table is referenced when the Assignment type is 'User Group Field', not 'User Field'.
The Task [task] table is the base table for tasks created by the policy, but it is not what the Task assignment dropdown references for User Field assignment.
Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] is the target table for the policy's data filter, not the table referenced for task assignment.

source.excerpt: User Field: Assigns policy tasks to a user in the user field specified in Task assignment. The drop-down list in Task assignment contains fields in the table set by the data filter, that reference the User [sys_user] table (such as Attested by and Assigned to).

questions.question: Which CMDB Data Manager lifecycle policy types require an active retirement definition for each targeted class? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Retire
Attestation
Archive
Certification
Delete

explanation.correct: The lifecycle policies Retire, Archive, and Delete all require that an active retirement definition exists for each targeted class in the policy. Without it, the policy creation fails with an error.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Attestation is a data management policy type that verifies CI data accuracy. It does not require a retirement definition since it does not involve lifecycle state changes.
Certification is a policy type that supports even non-CMDB tables and does not require a retirement definition.

source.excerpt: The life-cycle policies Retire, Archive, and Delete, require that an active retirement definition exists for each targeted class in the policy.

questions.question: In a scripted audit, which methods from SNC.CertificationProcessing are used to log the results of audited records? (Select TWO)

options.text: logAuditResultPass
logAuditResultWarning
createFollowOnTask
logAuditResultFail

explanation.correct: The SNC.CertificationProcessing class provides logAuditResultPass() to log a passing result and logAuditResultFail() to log a failing result for audited records. These are the two methods specifically for logging audit results.

wrongAnswers.explanation: logAuditResultWarning is not a method in the SNC.CertificationProcessing API. Audit results are logged as either pass or fail.
createFollowOnTask creates a remediation task for failed records, but it does not log audit results. It is a separate step from result logging.

source.excerpt: new SNC.CertificationProcessing().logAuditResultFail(current.sys_id, sysId, followOnTask, columnNameSpace, 'greater than', desiredFloorSpaceUsage, floorSpaceInUse, true); ... new SNC.CertificationProcessing().logAuditResultPass(current.sys_id, sysId, true);

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the main CI in the duplicate CIs remediation process?

options.text: It is the CI that was created most recently and has the latest data
It is the duplicate CI selected to retain as an active CI after reconciling the other duplicates into it
It is automatically chosen by the system as the CI with the most relationships
It is a new CI created by the system to replace all the duplicate CIs

explanation.correct: The main CI is one of the duplicate CIs that you want to retain as an active CI after reconciling the rest of the duplicate CIs into it. You can then potentially retire or delete the rest of the duplicate CIs, or assign custom values to their attributes. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The main CI is not automatically the most recently created CI. It is manually selected by the administrator during remediation.
The main CI is not automatically chosen based on relationships. The first step during remediation is for the administrator to select the main CI.
The main CI is not a newly created CI. It is one of the existing duplicate CIs that is selected to be retained.

source.excerpt: The main CI is one of the duplicate CIs that you want to retain as an active CI after reconciling the rest of the duplicate CIs into that main CI. You can then potentially retire or delete the rest of the duplicate CIs, or assign custom values to their attributes.

questions.question: What happens when a CI associated with a change request in 'New' state is deleted during duplicate CI remediation?

options.text: The change request is automatically canceled
The CI reference in the change request is updated to the main CI
The CI is removed from the change request and no replacement is made
The change request is placed on hold until a new CI is manually assigned

explanation.correct: When a CI is associated with a change request whose state is New, then when duplicate CI remediation processes delete the CI, the CI in the change request is updated to the main CI. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The change request is not canceled. For change requests in the New state, the CI reference is simply updated to the main CI.
This behavior applies to change requests that are NOT in the New state. For New change requests, the CI is updated to the main CI rather than just removed.
The change request is not placed on hold. The system automatically updates the CI reference to the main CI for change requests in New state.

source.excerpt: When a CI is associated with a change request whose state is New, then when duplicate CI remediation processes delete the CI, the CI in the change request is updated to the main CI.

questions.question: An administrator needs to remediate a de-duplication task that has over 1,200 duplicate CIs. The default threshold property glide.duplicate_ci_remediator.max.cis is set to 1,000. What should the administrator do to allow full reconciliation support for this task?

options.text: Increase the glide.duplicate_ci_remediator.max.cis property to at least 1,200
Enable the glide.duplicate_ci_remediator.enable_restricted_mode property
Split the de-duplication task into multiple smaller tasks manually
Set the glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates.threshold property to 1,200

explanation.correct: The threshold for full reconciliation support is based on the glide.duplicate_ci_remediator.max.cis property (default 1,000). You can update this property to increase the threshold up to a maximum of 5,000. Since 1,200 is under 5,000, increasing the property to at least 1,200 will restore full reconciliation options. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Restricted mode is used when a large number of related items blocks the remediation process due to loading timeouts, not for exceeding the duplicate CI count threshold.
There is no supported mechanism to manually split de-duplication tasks. The correct approach is to increase the max CIs property.
The skip_duplicates.threshold property controls how IRE processes duplicate CIs during identification, not the remediation wizard's reconciliation limits.

source.excerpt: This threshold is based on the value of the glide.duplicate_ci_remediator.max.cis property, which is 1,000 by default. You can update this property to increase the threshold. However, this threshold never exceeds 5,000, even if you set the property to a value greater than 5,000.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the De-duplication Template Library in CMDB Workspace?

options.text: To store a log of all previously completed de-duplication tasks for audit purposes
To create preconfigured de-duplication templates with remediation settings for a class that can be applied to multiple tasks in bulk
To automatically detect and flag duplicate CIs during the IRE process
To define identification rules that prevent duplicate CIs from being created

explanation.correct: The De-duplication Template Library in CMDB Workspace lets you create a preconfigured de-duplication template with the remediation settings for a class. The De-duplication dashboard then lets you run the preconfigured template on multiple de-duplication tasks for that class in bulk. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Template Library is not an audit log. It stores preconfigured templates for bulk remediation, not historical records of completed tasks.
Detecting duplicate CIs is done by the IRE (Identification and Reconciliation Engine), not by the De-duplication Template Library.
Identification rules that prevent duplicates are configured separately in the IRE. The Template Library is specifically for remediating existing duplicate CIs.

source.excerpt: The De-duplication Template Library in CMDB Workspace lets you create a preconfigured de-duplication template with the remediation settings for a class. The De-duplication dashboard in CMDB Workspace lets you then run the preconfigured template on multiple de-duplication tasks for the class that is set in the template.

questions.question: Which table stores the individual certification tasks created by the Data Certification plugin?

options.text: Certification Instance [cert_instance]
Certification Element [cert_element]
Certification Task [cert_task]
Certification Schedule [cert_schedule]

explanation.correct: The Certification Task [cert_task] table stores individual certification tasks. This table extends the Task table. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_InstalledWithDataCertification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Certification Instance [cert_instance] table stores a collection of certification tasks representing a single instance of a scheduled certification. It extends the Audit [cert_audit] table, but doesn't store individual tasks.
The Certification Element [cert_element] table stores the data elements that are grouped into certification tasks, not the tasks themselves.
The Certification Schedule [cert_schedule] table stores the schedule configuration for certifications, including what data to certify, assignment, and frequency — not the individual tasks.

source.excerpt: Certification Task [cert_task] — Stores individual certification tasks. Certification Task extends the Task table.

questions.question: Which TWO business rules does the Data Certification plugin add to the Certification Task [cert_task] table? (Select TWO)

options.text: Merge Certification Tasks — merges two tasks when a task is reassigned and another task for the same instance exists with the new user
Cancel Instance — cancels all open certification tasks when an active certification is canceled
Certification Instance Rollup — updates the Percent complete field on the certification instance record
Prevent delete of Filter with Schedule — prevents the deletion of a filter used in a schedule

explanation.correct: Both 'Merge Certification Tasks' and 'Certification Instance Rollup' are business rules on the Certification Task [cert_task] table. Merge Certification Tasks merges two tasks together when reassignment creates a duplicate, and Certification Instance Rollup updates the percent complete on the parent instance. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_InstalledWithDataCertification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Cancel Instance is a business rule on the Certification Instance [cert_instance] table, not on the Certification Task table.
Prevent delete of Filter with Schedule is a business rule on the Certification Filter [cert_filter] table, not on the Certification Task table.

source.excerpt: Merge Certification Tasks | Certification Task [cert_task] | Merges two tasks together when a task is reassigned and there is another task for the same instance with the new user. ... Certification Instance Rollup | Certification Task [cert_task] | Updates the Percent complete field on the certification instance record.

questions.question: What restriction is enforced on the duplicate_of field to ensure data integrity during duplicate CI remediation?

options.text: The duplicate_of field can only reference CIs in the same CMDB class
A CI cannot be set as a duplicate of another duplicate CI, preventing chains of duplicate references
The duplicate_of field is read-only and can only be set by the IRE process
The duplicate_of field must reference a CI that was created before the duplicate CI

explanation.correct: The duplicate_of attribute of the main CI cannot reference any CI as its main CI — you cannot set a CI as a duplicate of another duplicate CI to create a chain of duplicate CIs. If you attempt this, the system sets the CI as a duplicate of the main CI of the duplicate CI you're trying to set. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/de-duplication-tasks.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The restriction is about domain, not class. A CI and its main CI cannot be from different domains, but they are not required to be in the same class.

While manual updates to duplicate_of should be restricted, the field is not strictly read-only. The system enforces specific rules when modifications are attempted rather than completely preventing them.
There is no restriction based on creation date. The restrictions are: a CI cannot be its own duplicate, CIs must be in the same domain, and no chaining of duplicate references.

source.excerpt: The duplicate_of attribute of the main CI cannot reference any CI as its main CI (you cannot set a CI as a duplicate of another duplicate CI to create a chain of duplicate CIs).

questions.question: An administrator is configuring a new Data Certification schedule and needs to understand which UI policies affect the Certification Schedule form. Which TWO behaviors are controlled by UI policies on the Certification Schedule [cert_schedule] table? (Select TWO)

options.text: The Next Scheduled Run field is hidden when the schedule is set to run once or on demand only
The Percent complete field is made read-only when the state is Work in Progress
The Table field is made read-only on the schedule form
The Certification Task Elements formatter displays green check marks and red exclamation points

explanation.correct: Two UI policies on the Certification Schedule table are: 'Hide next scheduled run' which hides the Next Scheduled Run field when the schedule is set to run once or on demand only, and 'Make table name read only' which makes the Table field read-only on the schedule form. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/r_InstalledWithDataCertification.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The 'Make percent complete field read only' UI policy applies to the Certification Instance [cert_instance] table, not the Certification Schedule table.
The Certification Task Elements is a formatter, not a UI policy. It enables custom UI formatting on certification tasks but is a separate component type.

source.excerpt: Hide next scheduled run | Certification Schedule [cert_schedule] | Hides the Next Scheduled Run field when the schedule is set to run once or on demand only. ... Make table name read only | Certification Schedule [cert_schedule] | Makes the Table field read-only.

questions.question: When you select 'Enable life cycle sync' on the Life cycle mapping table list page, which system property is set to true?

options.text: csdm.lifecycle.migration.activated
csdm.lifecycle.sync.between.ci.and.asset.activated
csdm.lifecycle.bulk.alignment.enabled
csdm.lifecycle.mapping.sync.active

explanation.correct: Selecting 'Enable life cycle sync' sets the csdm.lifecycle.sync.between.ci.and.asset.activated system property to true, which initiates the align-and-sync process for CSDM life-cycle values.

wrongAnswers.explanation: csdm.lifecycle.migration.activated is the plugin name, not the system property that gets set when enabling life cycle sync.
csdm.lifecycle.bulk.alignment.enabled is not a real system property in this context. Bulk alignment is a phase of the process, not a separate property.
csdm.lifecycle.mapping.sync.active is a fabricated property name. The correct property specifically references the sync between CI and asset.

source.excerpt: To start the align and sync process, you select Enable life cycle sync on the Life cycle mapping table list page. That action sets the csdm.lifecycle.sync.between.ci.and.asset.activated system property to true and starts the following activities.

questions.question: Which table in ServiceNow holds the mapping rules that specify how legacy status values are converted to CSDM life-cycle value pairs?

options.text: cmdb_ci_lifecycle
alm_asset_ci_state_mapping
life_cycle_mapping
csdm_status_mapping

explanation.correct: The life_cycle_mapping table holds the mapping rules that define how legacy status values are aligned to CSDM life-cycle value pairs (life cycle stage and life cycle stage status). The base system includes default mapping rules in this table.

wrongAnswers.explanation: cmdb_ci_lifecycle is not the table that holds CSDM life-cycle mapping rules. The correct table is life_cycle_mapping.
alm_asset_ci_state_mapping is a legacy table used for asset-to-CI state mapping, not for mapping legacy values to CSDM life-cycle value pairs.
csdm_status_mapping is not a real ServiceNow table. The correct table for CSDM life-cycle mappings is life_cycle_mapping.

source.excerpt: The base system includes the life-cycle mapping [life_cycle_mapping] table that holds mapping rules. The default rules specify how to align common legacy status values to a CSDM life-cycle value pair.

questions.question: During Phase 2 of the CSDM life-cycle align-and-sync process, how are life-cycle values determined for a CI that is NOT associated with an asset?

options.text: The CI is skipped and retains only its legacy status values
The CI inherits life-cycle values from the closest related asset in the CMDB hierarchy
CSDM mapping tables are used to derive the CI's life-cycle values from its legacy status
The CI is flagged with a discrepancy error and requires manual remediation

explanation.correct: In Phase 2 Step 3, for CIs not associated with an asset, the system uses CSDM mapping tables to derive the CI's life-cycle value pair from its legacy status values. This is a one-time sync that won't be repeated because future values derive from bi-directional sync.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Non-asset CIs are not skipped. The system has a specific step (Step 3) in Phase 2 to handle CIs that are not associated with an asset.
The system does not use CMDB hierarchy inheritance for life-cycle values. For non-asset CIs, it uses the CSDM mapping tables directly against the CI's own legacy status.
Non-asset CIs do not generate discrepancy errors during Phase 2. Discrepancy checks occur in Phase 1, and Phase 2 handles the actual bulk alignment automatically.

source.excerpt: Step 3: One-time sync: If a CI is not associated with an asset, use CSDM mapping tables to derive the CI's life-cycle values from the legacy status.

questions.question: Which TWO changes occur during Phase 3 of the CSDM life-cycle align-and-sync process? (Select TWO)

options.text: Bi-directional sync of CSDM life-cycle value pairs between asset and CI is activated
All legacy status fields are permanently removed from the CI table
Bi-directional sync between CMDB CI legacy values and CSDM life-cycle values is deactivated
IBI records are migrated from the life_cycle_mapping table to the cmdb_ci table

explanation.correct: Phase 3 activates bi-directional sync of CSDM life-cycle value pairs between asset and CI, and deactivates the bi-directional sync between CMDB CI legacy values and CSDM life-cycle values. This means CI life-cycle values will now sync with asset life-cycle values instead of being derived from CI legacy values.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Legacy status fields are not removed. They continue to exist and the existing bi-directional sync between asset legacy values and CI legacy values continues. However, CI legacy values will diverge from CSDM life-cycle values over time.

IBI records are not migrated between tables during Phase 3. The documentation states that IBI records do not change during Phase 2 because active sync between legacy and life-cycle values for IBI records is already in place.

source.excerpt: New: Activate sync of life-cycle data between asset and CMDB CI — CSDM life-cycle value pairs are bi-directionally synced between asset and CI. New: Deactivate Bi-directional sync between CMDB CI legacy values and CSDM life-cycle values — As a result, changes to CI legacy values will not update CSDM life-cycle value pairs (the values will diverge over time).

questions.question: An administrator sets the Operational Status of a hardware CI to 'Retired' in the CMDB. What automatically happens to the CI's Status/Hardware Status field?

options.text: It is set to 'Non-Operational'
It remains unchanged and must be manually updated
It is automatically set to 'Retired'
It is set to 'Absent'

explanation.correct: In CI Lifecycle Management's integration with Asset Management, when the Operational Status of a CI is set to 'Retired', the Status/Hardware Status field is automatically set to 'Retired' as well. This synchronization keeps both fields consistent.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Non-Operational is the status set in the opposite scenario — when a CI's Status/Hardware Status changes FROM Retired to another status, then Operational Status is set to Non-Operational.
The fields are automatically synchronized when either is set to Retired. Manual intervention is not required for this specific transition.
Absent (install_status value 100) is a separate status used in install_status tracking. It is not the result of setting Operational Status to Retired.

source.excerpt: When Operational Status of a CI is set to Retired, then the Status/Hardware Status field is automatically set to Retired.

questions.question: In CMDB CI Lifecycle Management, what is the default behavior regarding Compatible CI Actions?

options.text: All CI actions within the same category are automatically compatible
No two actions for a CI are compatible with each other by default
All CI actions are compatible unless explicitly restricted
Compatibility is determined automatically based on the CI's operational state

explanation.correct: By default, there are no two actions for a CI that are compatible with each other. Administrators must explicitly define pairs of actions as compatible to allow them to be applied simultaneously to a CI.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CI actions do not have categories that determine compatibility. Compatibility must be explicitly configured by defining specific pairs of compatible actions.
This is the opposite of the default behavior. By default, no actions are compatible — you must explicitly specify compatible pairs.
Operational state does not automatically determine action compatibility. Compatibility is configured independently through the Compatible CI Actions rules.

source.excerpt: CI Lifecycle Management allows a CI to have multiple active CI actions simultaneously, however they must be specifically defined as compatible. By default, there are no two actions for a CI that are compatible with each other.

questions.question: Which TWO types of restrictions can be configured using the CI Lifecycle Management UI? (Select TWO)

options.text: Not Allowed CI Actions that prevent specific actions based on operational state
Maximum concurrent CI count limits per operational state
Not Allowed Operational Transitions between specific states for a CI type
Automatic CI archival rules when a CI reaches end-of-life state

explanation.correct: The CI Lifecycle Management UI allows you to configure Not Allowed CI Actions (restricting actions when a CI is in a specific operational state) and Not Allowed Operational Transitions (restricting transitions from one operational state to another for a specified CI type). These are two of the three configurable rule types alongside Compatible CI Actions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CI Lifecycle Management does not include limits on how many CIs can be in a particular operational state. It manages state transitions and action restrictions, not capacity.
Automatic CI archival is handled by the CMDB Data Manager, not by CI Lifecycle Management rules. CI Lifecycle Management focuses on operational state transitions and action restrictions.

source.excerpt: The CI Lifecycle Management UI lets you modify this default behavior by specifying Not Allowed CI Actions, Compatible CI Actions, and Not Allowed Operational Transitions that restricts some operations and enables for others.

questions.question: A non-workflow automation tool needs to use CI Lifecycle Management APIs to apply CI actions. What must the tool do before performing any lifecycle operations?

options.text: Create a record in the Compatible CI Actions table for the target CI
Call the registerOperator API to obtain a unique requestor ID
Submit a change request referencing the target CI
Set the CI's operational status to 'Operational' before applying any actions

explanation.correct: Non-workflow requestors must call the registerOperator API to register and obtain a requestor ID (a unique GUID) before using lifecycle management APIs. Workflow users can use the active Workflow context as the requestor ID and do not need to explicitly call registerOperator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Compatible CI Actions define which pairs of actions can be applied simultaneously to a CI. They are configured by administrators as rules, not created per-operation by automation tools.
While Change Management can use CI Lifecycle Management as a mechanism, submitting a change request is not a prerequisite for using the lifecycle management APIs.

There is no requirement to set a CI to 'Operational' before applying actions. Actions can be applied based on operational state rules, and the CI's current state is what determines which actions are allowed.

source.excerpt: To register and to obtain a requestor ID, non-workflow users should call the registerOperator API. Workflow users can use the active Workflow context as the requestor ID, and they do not need to explicitly call registerOperator.

questions.question: In the context of CMDB Health domain separation, which statement is true about global system properties that control CMDB Health?

options.text: They are domain separated and can be overridden per subdomain
They are not domain separated
They are stored in the cmdb_health_metric_pref table
They require the Domain Extensions Installer plugin to function

explanation.correct: Global system properties that control CMDB Health are not domain separated. They apply uniformly across all domains. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-health-domain-separation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: System properties are not domain separated. Health Metrics settings (stored in cmdb_health_metric_pref) are domain separated, but system properties are not.
The cmdb_health_metric_pref table stores Health Metrics preferences, which are domain separated. Global system properties are a separate configuration.
The Domain Extensions Installer plugin enables domain awareness for the CMDB Health dashboard, but system properties exist independently of this plugin.

source.excerpt: Global system properties that control CMDB Health – System properties are not domain separated.

questions.question: Starting with the Tokyo release, how are CIs in the global domain evaluated when viewed from a subdomain in CMDB Health?

options.text: They are evaluated against both global and subdomain local metric tests
They are excluded from health evaluations when viewed in subdomains
They are evaluated only against metric tests specified in the global domain
They are evaluated against subdomain local metric tests only

explanation.correct: Starting with the Tokyo release, CIs in the global domain are evaluated only against metric tests specified in the global domain. Subdomain local metric tests are applied only to CIs in that subdomain, not to global domain CIs—even though global CIs are visible in the subdomain. This change prevents excessive duplicated data. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-health-domain-separation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This was the behavior before the Tokyo release (up until San Diego). Subdomain local metric tests were previously applied to global domain CIs, which could generate large amounts of duplicated data.
Global domain CIs are still visible in subdomains and their health results do appear on subdomain dashboards. They are not excluded—they are simply evaluated only against global domain tests.
The opposite is true. Global domain CIs are evaluated against global domain tests only, not subdomain tests. Subdomain local metric tests apply only to CIs in that subdomain.

source.excerpt: Starting with the Tokyo release, CIs in the global domain are evaluated only against metric tests specified in the global domain. In subdomains, local metric tests are applied only to the CIs in that subdomain and are not applied to the global domain CIs (even though the global domain CIs are visible in the subdomain).

questions.question: An administrator notices that CMDB Health dashboard jobs are taking an excessively long time to complete. The instance has over 100 active domains. What is the recommended approach to improve job performance?

options.text: Create separate dashboard jobs for each domain to distribute the workload
Increase the job frequency so each run processes fewer changes
Set Active to false for all root domains, disabling all domains in the hierarchy
Disable domain separation to consolidate all CIs into a single domain

explanation.correct: The Active setting is the most important because it affects how long jobs run. When there is a large number of domains (>100), the job can take a very long time. The recommended mitigation is to set Active to false for all root domains, thereby disabling all other domains in the hierarchy. Then selectively enable only the domains needed. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-health-domain-separation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is a single dashboard job for each major KPI (such as Completeness) that runs across all enabled domains. Jobs themselves are not domain separated, so you cannot create separate jobs per domain.
Increasing the frequency would cause the long-running job to execute more often, making the problem worse. The root cause is the number of active domains, not the frequency.
Disabling domain separation entirely would remove important data governance controls. The correct approach is to strategically manage which domains are set to Active.

source.excerpt: If there is a large number of domains (>100) the job can take a very long time. To mitigate this, set Active to false for all the root domains, thereby disabling all the other domains in the hierarchy. If there is a rule at the top, all child domains inherit that rule.

questions.question: Which of the following CMDB Health-related rules are domain separated? (Select TWO)

options.text: Required fields for Completeness
Recommended fields for Completeness
Duplicate identification rules for Correctness
Orphan rules for Correctness

explanation.correct: Recommended fields are domain separated (stored in the CMDB Recommended Fields [cmdb_recommended_fields] table, which is domain separated). Orphan rules are also domain separated (stored in the CMDB Health Orphan Rule [cmdb_health_orphan_rule] table, which is domain separated). See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-health-domain-separation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Required fields are based on the class schema defined in the platform's System Dictionary and are fixed for all domains. They cannot be changed and are not domain separated.
Duplicates are based on Identification rules, which are not domain separated. The same duplicate identification rules apply to all domains.

source.excerpt: Required fields – These are based on the class schema defined in the platform's System dictionary and is fixed for all domains. These cannot be changed. Recommended fields – These are domain separated. Duplicates – Duplicates are based on Identification rules, which are not domain separated. Orphan – Orphan rules are domain separated.

questions.question: What is the correct navigation path to create a new certification schedule in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > CMDB > Data Certification > Schedules
All > Data Certification > Schedule Definitions
All > Configuration > Certification > Schedule Setup
All > Governance > Data Certification > New Schedule

explanation.correct: The correct navigation path to define a certification schedule is All > Data Certification > Schedule Definitions, then click New and fill in the required fields. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_DefiningACertificationSchedule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data Certification is its own application module, not nested under the CMDB module. The correct path is All > Data Certification > Schedule Definitions.
This is not a valid navigation path. Certification schedules are found under Data Certification > Schedule Definitions.
This is not a valid navigation path. Data Certification is a top-level module, not nested under a Governance module.

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Data Certification > Schedule Definitions.

questions.question: When defining a certification schedule, the Table field is read-only. How can an administrator change which table's records are certified?

options.text: Edit the Table field directly after unlocking it with the admin role
Select a different Filter or create a new Filter
Modify the Certification fields selection to reference a different table
Change the Assignment type to point to a different table

explanation.correct: The Table field on a certification schedule is read-only and displays the table holding the records to be certified. To change the table, an administrator must select a different Filter or create a new Filter, which determines the table. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_DefiningACertificationSchedule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Table field is strictly read-only and cannot be directly edited, even with the admin role. The table is derived from the selected Filter.
Certification fields specify which fields on the table require certification. They do not control which table is used—that is determined by the Filter.
The Assignment type controls how certification tasks are assigned to users or groups. It does not affect which table's records are being certified.

source.excerpt: Table: [Read-only] The table holding the records to be certified. To change the table name, select a different Filter or create a new Filter.

questions.question: An administrator needs to create a certification schedule where tasks are assigned to the user listed in each CI's 'Managed by' field. If the 'Managed by' field is empty on a record, no certification task should be created for that record. Which configuration should the administrator use?

options.text: Assignment type: Specific User, and manually select the Managed by user
Assignment type: User Field, Assign to: Managed by, Assign to empty: Create Unassigned Task
Assignment type: User Field, Assign to: Managed by, Assign to empty: Do Not Create Task
Assignment type: Group Field, Assign to group: Managed by, Assign to empty: Do Not Create Task

explanation.correct: The User Field assignment type allows selecting a user reference field (such as 'Managed by') on the table being certified. Setting 'Assign to empty' to 'Do Not Create Task' ensures no task is created when the Managed by field is empty on a record. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/t_DefiningACertificationSchedule.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Specific User assigns one specific user to ALL certification tasks for the schedule. It does not dynamically assign tasks based on the Managed by field of each record.

While the Assignment type and Assign to settings are correct, 'Create Unassigned Task' would still create tasks for records with an empty Managed by field—they would just be unassigned. The requirement states no task should be created.
Group Field is used for group reference fields, not user reference fields. 'Managed by' is a user reference field, so User Field is the correct assignment type.

source.excerpt: User Field: Select a user reference field on the table being certified. As an example, select the user named in the Managed by field to identify the user who performs the task. Do Not Create Task: No task is created when the Assign to or Assign to group field is empty.

questions.question: When the Domain Support — Domain Extensions Installer plugin is activated, which statements are true about the CMDB Health dashboard? (Select TWO)

options.text: Separate dashboard jobs are created for each domain to improve performance
The dashboard aggregates and reports health failures based on the user's domain visibility of CIs
Users can configure KPI and metric settings specific to their domain, such as active/inactive and thresholds
Child domains must independently configure their own health configurations and cannot inherit from parent domains

explanation.correct: When the Domain Extensions Installer plugin is activated, the CMDB Health dashboard becomes domain aware. It aggregates and reports health failures and scores based on the user's domain visibility of CIs, and users can configure KPI and metric settings specific to their domain (such as active/inactive and thresholds). See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/cmdb-health-domain-separation.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is a single dashboard job for each major KPI that finds the health of CIs across all enabled domains. Jobs are not domain separated—there is only one job run for all domains.

A child domain derives its immediate parent's domain health configurations if the child domain does not configure its own. Child domains can optionally override parent configurations, but they inherit by default.

source.excerpt: The CMDB Health dashboard aggregates and reports health failures and scores based on user's domain visibility of CIs. Users can configure KPI and metric settings specific to the needs in their domain. So different domains can have different settings such as active/inactive, and thresholds. A child domain derives its immediate parent's domain health configurations if the child domain does not configure its own.

questions.question: Which role is required to create a compliance audit in ServiceNow?

options.text: certification
certification_admin
certification_filter_admin
itil

explanation.correct: The certification_admin role is required to create a compliance audit. This role can manage the entire certification process, including creating, editing, and deleting all certification records. The documentation explicitly states 'Role required: certification_admin' as a prerequisite.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The certification role only allows users to read and update certification tasks to resolve discrepancies. It does not grant the ability to create audits.
The certification_filter_admin role allows creating, reading, and updating certification filters, but not managing the full audit lifecycle.
The itil role grants the certification role automatically when the Certification Core plugin is activated, but the itil role itself does not provide audit creation privileges.

source.excerpt: Role required: certification_admin

questions.question: Which table stores the definition of the desired state of a record, including the filter that identifies records to evaluate and expected attribute and relationship values?

options.text: Audit [cert_audit]
Audit Result [cert_audit_result]
Certification Template [cert_template]
Certification Condition [cert_cond]

explanation.correct: The Certification Template [cert_template] table contains the definition of the desired state of the record. The template includes a filter that identifies the records to evaluate and the expected attributes and relationship values.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Audit [cert_audit] table contains the data required to run an audit, including users assigned to follow-on tasks and the run schedule, but not the desired state definition itself.
The Audit Result [cert_audit_result] table contains the results of specific certification audits after they run, not the desired state definition.

The Certification Condition [cert_cond] table is the base table that defines individual desired attribute or relationship conditions, but the overall desired state definition including the filter is stored in the Certification Template.

source.excerpt: Certification Template [cert_template] — Contains the definition of the desired state of the record. The template includes a filter that identifies the records to evaluate and the expected attributes and relationship values.

questions.question: When the Certification Core plugin is activated, what happens when a user who has the certification role also has a manager specified on their user record?

options.text: The manager is automatically assigned the certification_admin role
The manager is automatically granted the certification role
The certification role is propagated to all users up the management chain
The manager must manually request the certification role through a catalog item

explanation.correct: When both a manager and the certification role are specified for a user, the system automatically grants the certification role to the manager. This ensures that a certification task can be escalated successfully to the next level. The automatic role is granted to the user's immediate manager only.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The manager receives the certification role, not the certification_admin role. The certification_admin role must be explicitly assigned and is not automatically propagated.
The system grants the automatic role to the user's immediate manager only and not to others up the management chain.
The certification role is granted automatically to the manager via business rules (Add Certification Role To Manager), not through a manual request process.

source.excerpt: When both a manager and the certification role are specified for a user, the system automatically grants the certification role to the manager. This functionality ensures that a certification task can be escalated successfully to the next level. The system grants this automatic role to the user's immediate manager only and not to others up the management chain.

questions.question: A CMDB administrator is configuring a compliance audit and wants follow-on tasks to be assigned to the person listed in the Managed by field on each failed CI record. If the Managed by field is empty on a specific CI, the administrator wants an unassigned task created so it can be manually assigned later. Which combination of settings should the administrator configure?

options.text: Assignment type: Specific User, and select a fallback user
Assignment type: User Field, Assign to: Managed by, Assign to empty: Create Unassigned Task
Assignment type: User Field, Assign to: Managed by, Assign to empty: Do Not Create Task
Assignment type: Group Field, Assign to group: Support group, Assign to empty: Create Assigned Task

explanation.correct: The User Field assignment type allows selecting a user reference field (like Managed by) on the table being audited. Setting Assign to empty to 'Create Unassigned Task' creates a follow-on task without assigning it to any user when the field is blank, allowing manual assignment later.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Specific User assigns all tasks to one designated user, regardless of the CI record's field values. It does not dynamically use the Managed by field on each CI.

While this correctly uses User Field with Managed by, setting Assign to empty to 'Do Not Create Task' means no follow-on task would be created when the Managed by field is empty. The requirement specifies an unassigned task should still be created.

Group Field is used for group reference fields (like Support group), not user reference fields like Managed by. Additionally, Create Assigned Task would assign to a specific group rather than leaving the task unassigned.

source.excerpt: User Field: Select a user reference field on the table being audited. For example, you choose the user identified in the Managed by field on the failed record to perform the tasks. ... Create Unassigned Task: Create a follow-on task, but do not assign it to any user or group. The task can be manually assigned later.

questions.question: Which TWO types of certification condition tables extend the base Certification Condition [cert_cond] table in the Compliance Certification Core? (Select TWO)

options.text: Certification Attribute Condition [cert_attr_cond]
Certification Audit Schedule [cert_audit_schedule]
Certification CI Relationship Condition [cert_ci_rel_cond]
Certification Task Assignment [cert_task_assign]

explanation.correct: Both the Certification Attribute Condition [cert_attr_cond] and Certification CI Relationship Condition [cert_ci_rel_cond] tables extend the base Certification Condition [cert_cond] table. Other tables that also extend it include cert_user_rel_cond, cert_group_rel_cond, and cert_related_list_cond.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Certification Audit Schedule is not a table installed with the Certification Core plugin. Audit scheduling is configured directly within the Audit [cert_audit] record using Run, Day, and Time fields.

Certification Task Assignment is not a table installed with the Certification Core plugin. Task assignments are managed through the Follow On Task [cert_follow_on_task] table and the audit's assignment type settings.

source.excerpt: Certification Attribute Condition [cert_attr_cond] — Contains the conditions that define the desired CI attribute values. This table extends the Certification Condition [cert_cond] base table. Certification CI Relationship Condition [cert_ci_rel_cond] — Contains the CI to CI relationship conditions. This table extends the Certification Condition [cert_cond] base table.

questions.question: What are the default values for the Health window and Threshold count fields when creating a new compliance audit?

options.text: Health window: 30 Days, Threshold count: 10
Health window: 7 Days, Threshold count: 5
Health window: 7 Hours, Threshold count: 3
Health window: 14 Days, Threshold count: 5

explanation.correct: The default value for the Health window field is 7, with the default Health window unit being Days. The default value for the Threshold count is 5. Together these define a 7-day evaluation period where up to 5 audit failures are acceptable before the threshold is exceeded.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The default health window is 7 days, not 30 days, and the default threshold count is 5, not 10.
While Hours is a valid health window unit, the default unit is Days, not Hours. The threshold count defaults to 5, not 3.
The default health window is 7 days, not 14 days. The threshold count of 5 is correct, but the health window value is wrong.

source.excerpt: Health window — The default value for this field is 7. Health window unit — The default value for this field is Days. Threshold count — The default value for the threshold is 5.

questions.question: An administrator attempts to delete an audit record that has been previously run. The Delete option is disabled. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The audit record is still in an Active state
The audit record has existing audit results
The administrator only has the certification role, not certification_admin
The audit is linked to a scheduled job that is currently running

explanation.correct: ServiceNow prevents deletion of an audit containing results. A business rule called 'Prevent deletion of audit with results' enforces this restriction. Similarly, audit results that have follow-on tasks cannot be deleted. The Delete option is disabled in records and lists where these dependent records exist.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Active state of an audit controls whether it runs on schedule, but does not prevent deletion. The restriction is specifically about having dependent audit results.

While the certification role alone cannot manage all certification records, the question states the Delete option is disabled (not access denied), which points to the business rule preventing deletion of audits with results.
A currently running scheduled job does not disable the Delete option on the audit record. The deletion prevention is enforced by a business rule that checks for existing audit results.

source.excerpt: You cannot delete audit records that have audit results or audit results that have follow-on tasks. ServiceNow disables the Delete option in records and lists where these dependent records exist.

questions.question: An administrator wants to create a compliance audit using the CI Class Manager. Which steps are required to access the audit creation form from the CI Class Manager? (Select TWO)

options.text: Select a class from the Class Hierarchy
Navigate to the Health Dashboard and select the Compliance tab
In the sidebar, check Advanced and then select Audit in the Compliance group
Right-click the class and choose Create Compliance Audit from the context menu

explanation.correct: To create a compliance audit via the CI Class Manager, you first navigate to All > Configuration > CI Class Manager, then select a class from the Class Hierarchy. In the sidebar, you check Advanced and then select Audit in the Compliance group. This opens the audit creation interface for the selected class.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Health Dashboard is used for monitoring CMDB health KPIs and scores, not for creating compliance audits. Audit creation is accessed through the CI Class Manager sidebar or the Compliance navigation modules.
There is no context menu option to create a compliance audit by right-clicking a class. The correct path is through the sidebar's Advanced checkbox and the Compliance group's Audit option.

source.excerpt: Use the CI Class Manager: Navigate to All > Configuration > CI Class Manager. Select a class from the Class Hierarchy. In the sidebar, check Advanced and then select Audit in the Compliance group.

questions.question: Which role provides full access to policies in the CMDB Data Manager, including the ability to create, edit, delete policies, and manage exclusion lists?

options.text: cmdb_admin
data_manager_user
data_manager_admin
itil_admin

explanation.correct: The data_manager_admin role provides full access to all features in the CMDB Data Manager, including full access to assigned tasks and policies, the ability to associate subflow categories to policy types, and the ability to create, edit, delete policies, calculate previews, approve tasks, and manage exclusion lists. This role contains data_manager_user, task_editor, and cmdb_query_builder_read.

wrongAnswers.explanation: cmdb_admin is a CMDB administration role but is not the specific role for CMDB Data Manager policy management.
data_manager_user can only view policies in read-only mode and calculate previews. It cannot create, edit, or delete policies.
itil_admin is not a valid ServiceNow role related to CMDB Data Manager.

source.excerpt: CMDB Data Manager administrator[data_manager_admin] — Can access all features in the CMDB Data Manager, including: Full access to assigned tasks. Full access to policies. Ability to associate subflow categories to policy type. Can create, edit, and delete policies, calculate previews, approve tasks, and manage exclusion lists.

questions.question: What is the default number of days that archived CIs are retained in archive tables before they are permanently deleted, as defined by the glide.cmdb.data_manager.default_archive_time property?

options.text: 30 days
60 days
90 days
120 days

explanation.correct: The glide.cmdb.data_manager.default_archive_time property controls how many days archived CIs can be restored from archive tables before permanent deletion. The default value is 120 days.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 30 days is the default for the sn_cmdb_ws.glide.cmdb.data.manager.aging.policy.task.timeframe property (aging policy task timeframe), not archive retention.
60 days is not a default value for any CMDB Data Manager property.
90 days is the default for the cmdb.data.manager.stale.task.life.in.days property (stale task threshold), not archive retention.

source.excerpt: glide.cmdb.data_manager.default_archive_time — Number of days that it is still possible to restore archived CIs from archive tables. After the specified number of days pass, archived CIs are permanently deleted from the archive tables. Type: Integer, Default value: 120

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are scheduled jobs related to CMDB Data Manager? (Select TWO)

options.text: CMDB Data Manager Retire Policy Processor
CMDB Health Audit Scheduled Job
CMDB Data Manager - Stale Task Cleaner
CMDB Discovery Reconciliation Engine

explanation.correct: CMDB Data Manager includes four scheduled jobs: CMDB Data Manager Archive/Delete Policy Processor, CMDB Data Manager Retire Policy Processor, CMDB Data Manager - Stale Task Cleaner, and CMDB Data Manager Delete Related Entry Policy Processor. The Retire Policy Processor processes all published policies of type Retire, applying them only to CIs that are not retired. The Stale Task Cleaner sets stale tasks (open and unapproved after 90 days by default) to Closed Cancelled.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CMDB Health Audit Scheduled Job is related to CMDB Health monitoring, not to CMDB Data Manager policy processing.
CMDB Discovery Reconciliation Engine is not a CMDB Data Manager scheduled job. Discovery reconciliation is handled by different CMDB components.

source.excerpt: Scheduled jobs: CMDB Data Manager Archive/Delete Policy Processor, CMDB Data Manager Retire Policy Processor, CMDB Data Manager - Stale Task Cleaner, CMDB Data Manager Delete Related Entry Policy Processor.

questions.question: How does the Attestation policy type in CMDB Data Manager differ from other policy types such as Delete or Retire?

options.text: It cannot be scheduled to run on a recurring basis
It does not support condition filters for targeting CIs
It is not associated with a subflow
It does not generate policy tasks for assigned users

explanation.correct: The Attestation policy type is unique because it is not associated with a subflow. For Attestation policies, a user must manually process all CIs in the task and submit the task to close it, unlike other policy types where the subflow automatically closes the task after completion.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Attestation policies can be scheduled with a frequency and start time, just like other policy types.
Attestation policies use the same condition filter mechanism as other policy types to specify target CIs.
Attestation policies do generate tasks. Attestation tasks are assigned to users as specified and appear in CMDB Workspace when those users log in.

source.excerpt: The Attestation policy type is not associated with a subflow. For an Attestation policy (which is not associated with a subflow), a user must process all CIs in the task and submit the task to close it.

questions.question: When the CMDB Data Manager Archive/Delete Policy Processor scheduled job runs, in what order does it process published policies?

options.text: It processes Delete policies first, then Archive policies
It processes all Archive policies first, and if no errors are encountered, continues to process Delete policies
It processes Archive and Delete policies simultaneously in parallel
It alternates between Archive and Delete policies based on their priority and creation date

explanation.correct: The CMDB Data Manager Archive/Delete Policy Processor processes all Archive policies first. Only if no errors are encountered during the Archive processing does it continue to process any Delete policies. This ensures data integrity by completing archival before permanent deletion. Both policy types apply only to CIs that are already retired.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The order is reversed — Archive policies are processed first, not Delete policies. This protects against data loss by ensuring archival completes successfully before deletion.
Archive and Delete policies are not processed in parallel. Archive policies must complete without errors before Delete policies begin.
The processor does not alternate or use priority-based ordering. It follows a strict sequence: all Archive policies first, then all Delete policies.

source.excerpt: CMDB Data Manager Archive/Delete Policy Processor — Processes all published polices of type Archive and Delete: Applies policies only to CIs that are already retired. Processes all Archive policies first, and if no errors encountered, continues to process any Delete policies.

questions.question: When a CMDB Data Manager policy of type Archive or Delete is evaluated, what happens to CIs that match the policy's condition filters but are not yet in a retired state?

options.text: They are automatically retired first, then processed by the Archive or Delete policy
They are added to the policy's CI exclusion list for future processing
They are not targeted for the policy
They are flagged with an error and notification is sent to the Data Manager administrator

explanation.correct: For Archive and Delete policy types, CIs that meet the policy filters but are not retired according to the class retirement definitions are simply not targeted for the policy. Retirement is a prerequisite — these policy types require that an active retirement definition exists for each targeted class, and only already-retired CIs are included in the policy execution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CIs are not automatically retired. Retirement must happen through a separate Retire policy or manual process before Archive or Delete policies can apply to them.
Non-retired CIs are not added to the exclusion list. They are simply not included in the target CI set. The exclusion list is used for explicitly excluding specific CIs that do meet all criteria.
Non-retired CIs matching the filter are expected behavior, not an error condition. They are silently excluded from the policy's target set.

source.excerpt: CIs that meet the policy filters but aren't retired according to the class retirement definitions, aren't targeted for the policy. If the policy type is archive or delete, CIs that meet the policy filters but are not retired, are not targeted for the policy.

questions.question: A CMDB administrator wants to configure a CMDB Data Manager policy so that policy tasks require review and approval before the associated subflow executes. Which TWO requirements must be met to enable this? (Select TWO)

options.text: The Needs Review checkbox must be checked on the policy definition
The policy type must be set to Attestation
The Managed By Group attribute must be populated in the target CIs
The Apply Retention Time field must be configured on the policy

explanation.correct: Two things must be in place: (1) The Needs Review checkbox must be checked on the policy to require review and approval of policy tasks. (2) The Managed By Group attribute must be populated in target CIs so that email notifications can be sent to members of that group for approval. Assigned users must also have the privilege to approve the policy tasks. When configured, a policy task triggers its subflow only after the task is approved.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Attestation policies are not associated with a subflow and have their own review process. The Needs Review option applies to other policy types like Delete, Archive, and Retire.
The Apply Retention Time field controls how long archived CIs are retained before permanent deletion. It is unrelated to the review and approval process for policy tasks.

source.excerpt: To require a review and an approval for a policy task: Ensure that the Managed By Group attribute is populated in target CIs and that the assigned users have the privilege to approve the policy tasks. Needs Review — Check to require a review and an approval of the policy tasks, by the group assignment in CIs' Managed by Group attribute or by an administrator. Otherwise, all policy tasks are approved automatically.

questions.question: An administrator creates an attestation policy in CMDB Data Manager that targets 30,000 CIs. After publishing the policy, how does CMDB Data Manager handle the task generation?

options.text: The policy is rejected because it exceeds the maximum number of CIs allowed per policy
A single attestation task is created containing all 30,000 CIs
Three attestation tasks are automatically created, each targeting 10,000 CIs
The administrator must manually split the CIs into separate policies before publishing

explanation.correct: CMDB Data Manager limits the number of target CIs per task to 10,000. When a policy targets more than 10,000 CIs, Data Manager automatically creates as many additional tasks as needed. In this case, 30,000 CIs are automatically split into three tasks of 10,000 CIs each. This is handled transparently without requiring manual intervention from the administrator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no maximum CI limit per policy. The 10,000 limit applies per task, and Data Manager automatically creates additional tasks to accommodate all CIs.
A single task cannot contain more than 10,000 CIs. Data Manager enforces the 10,000 CI per task limit by automatically splitting into multiple tasks.
Manual splitting is not required. Data Manager automatically creates multiple tasks when the number of target CIs exceeds 10,000 per task.

source.excerpt: CMDB Data Manager limits the number of target CIs per task to 10,000. Therefore, when a task exceeds that number, Data Manager automatically creates as many additional tasks as needed to include all the CIs for the task. For example, if you target 30,000 CIs in an attestation task, Data Manager breaks down that task into three tasks, each targeting 10,000 CIs.

questions.question: Which role is required to cancel an attestation task in CMDB Data Manager?
