data_manager_admin
sn_cmdb_user
itil

explanation.correct: Canceling an attestation task requires the data_manager_admin or sn_cmdb_admin role. This action is only available for tasks in the 'In progress' or 'Not started' status.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The data_manager_user role allows CI and service owners to review and process attestation tasks, but it does not grant permission to cancel them.
The sn_cmdb_user role includes the data_manager_user role for attestation task processing, but canceling tasks requires admin-level privileges.
The itil role is a general ITSM role and does not provide CMDB Data Manager attestation task management capabilities.

source.excerpt: Canceling an attestation task is available only for tasks that are in the 'In progress' or 'Not started' status, and the required role is data_manager_admin or sn_cmdb_admin.

questions.question: What are the three Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that CMDB Health calculates aggregated scores for?

options.text: Accuracy, Completeness, and Timeliness
Correctness, Compliance, and Completeness
Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability
Integrity, Consistency, and Completeness

explanation.correct: CMDB Health calculates an aggregated score for three KPIs: Correctness, Compliance, and Completeness. Each KPI further consists of sub-metrics that can be configured for inclusion in health evaluations and dashboards.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Accuracy and Timeliness are general data quality concepts but are not the named KPIs in CMDB Health. The correct KPIs are Correctness, Compliance, and Completeness.
Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) are hardware quality metrics, not CMDB Health KPIs.
While Completeness is one of the three correct KPIs, Integrity and Consistency are not named KPIs in CMDB Health. The other two are Correctness and Compliance.

source.excerpt: CMDB Health calculates an aggregated score for three Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) which are correctness, compliance, and completeness, each further consisting of sub-metrics.

questions.question: What is the default Effective Duration defined by the base system staleness rule for the Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class?

options.text: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days

explanation.correct: The base system includes a default staleness rule for the Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class which sets the Effective Duration time to 60 days. This rule applies to all extended CMDB classes and can be overridden by class-specific staleness rules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 30 days is not the default staleness duration. The base system default is 60 days for the cmdb_ci class.
45 days is not the default staleness duration. The base system default is 60 days for the cmdb_ci class.
90 days is not the default staleness duration. The base system default is 60 days for the cmdb_ci class.

source.excerpt: The base system includes a default staleness rule for the Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class, which sets the Effective Duration time to 60 days. This rule applies to all extended CMDB classes, and can be overridden by class specific staleness rules defined by the user.

questions.question: In CMDB Health, under which conditions is a CI determined to be an orphan?

options.text: The CI has not been updated within the staleness Effective Duration period
The CI satisfies the criteria in an orphan rule, or data is missing for the CI in its respective table or a parent table
The CI has duplicate identification rules matching other CIs in the same class
The CI has unpopulated mandatory fields defined in the system dictionary

explanation.correct: A CI is determined to be orphan if it satisfies the criteria in an orphan rule (which checks for specific attributes and missing relationships), or if data is missing for the CI in its respective table or in one of its parents' tables. An orphan CI is one that was unintentionally left in the CMDB when it is no longer needed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A CI not updated within the Effective Duration period is classified as stale, not orphan. Staleness is a separate sub-metric under the Correctness KPI.
CIs matching duplicate identification rules are measured by the Duplicate metric, not the Orphan metric. Both are sub-metrics of Correctness but measure different conditions.
CIs with unpopulated mandatory fields are measured by the Required metric under the Completeness KPI, not the Orphan metric under Correctness.

source.excerpt: A CI is determined to be orphan if: The CI satisfies the criteria in an orphan rule. This criteria checks for specific attributes that a CI must have, and for CIs that have no relationships or that don't have specific relationships. Data is missing for the CI in its respective table, or in one of its parents' table.

questions.question: During an attestation task review in CMDB Workspace, what happens when a CI owner excludes CIs from the task?

options.text: The CIs are moved to the Rejected CIs list and flagged for administrator review
The CIs are permanently retired from the CMDB and marked as decommissioned
The CIs are added to the exclusion list of CMDB Data Manager attestation policies
The CIs are reassigned to a different attestation task for a different CI owner

explanation.correct: When CIs are excluded from an attestation task, they are added to the exclusion list of CMDB Data Manager attestation policies. This means they will not be included in the current task or in future attestation policies. Only an admin can undo this operation using the CMDB Data Manager.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Excluded CIs are not moved to the Rejected CIs list. Rejection is a separate action that moves CIs to the Rejected list. Exclusion adds them to the policy exclusion list instead.
Excluding a CI from an attestation task does not retire or delete it from the CMDB. It only adds the CI to the exclusion list so it is not included in future attestation policies.
Excluded CIs are not reassigned to different tasks. They are removed from the current task and added to the attestation policy exclusion list to prevent inclusion in future tasks.

source.excerpt: Select the CIs that shouldn't be included in this task and in future Data Manager attestation policies, and click Exclude. Those excluded CIs are added to the exclusion list of CMDB Data Manager attestation policies. Only an admin can undo this operation using the CMDB Data Manager.

questions.question: Which of the following are sub-metrics of the Correctness KPI in CMDB Health? (Select TWO)

options.text: Required
Orphan
Audit
Staleness

explanation.correct: The Correctness KPI is an aggregation of three sub-metrics: Orphan (percentage of orphan CIs), Staleness (percentage of stale CIs), and Duplicate (percentage of duplicate CIs). Both Orphan and Staleness are correct sub-metrics of Correctness.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Required is a sub-metric of the Completeness KPI, not Correctness. It measures the percentage of CIs with unpopulated mandatory fields.
Audit is a sub-metric of the Compliance KPI, not Correctness. It compares actual CI field values against expected values defined in template and scripted audits.

source.excerpt: Correctness - A KPI which is an aggregation of the following metrics: Orphan... Staleness... Duplicate

questions.question: A CI owner is reviewing an attestation task and identifies several CIs that are duplicates of other CIs. What action should they take, and what is the result?

options.text: Click Reject to move the duplicate CIs to the Rejected CIs list and manually create a de-duplication task
Click Remove duplicates from task, which removes the CIs from the attestation task and automatically generates a de-duplication task
Click Exclude to add the duplicate CIs to the attestation policy exclusion list and flag them for deletion
Click Unattest to move the duplicate CIs back to the Not Yet Reviewed list and notify the CMDB administrator

explanation.correct: When duplicate CIs are identified during attestation review, the CI owner should select them and click 'Remove duplicates from task'. This removes those CIs from the attestation task and automatically generates a de-duplication task, similar to those created by the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE). Only an admin can undo this operation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Rejecting CIs is for CIs whose physical existence cannot be attested. It moves them to the Rejected list but does not create a de-duplication task. The correct action for duplicates is 'Remove duplicates from task'.

Excluding CIs removes them from the task and future attestation policies, but does not generate de-duplication tasks or flag them for deletion. This action is for CIs that shouldn't be part of attestation at all.
Unattest is used to move previously attested or rejected CIs back to the Not Yet Reviewed list. It is not the appropriate action for handling duplicate CIs.

source.excerpt: Select any CIs that you identify as duplicates of other CIs and click Remove duplicates from task. Those duplicate CIs are removed from the attestation task and a de-duplication task is generated for them, which is similar to the de-duplication tasks created by the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).

questions.question: A CMDB administrator is analyzing relationship health in the CMDB Health dashboard and notices several relationships failing health checks. Which of the following are relationship health metrics reported by CMDB Health? (Select TWO)

options.text: Incomplete relationships
Orphan relationships
Stale relationships
Expired relationships

explanation.correct: CMDB Health measures the health of CI relationships using three non-configurable metrics: Duplicate relationships, Orphan relationships, and Stale relationships. A single relationship can fail more than one health test — for example, a duplicate relationship can also be stale.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incomplete relationships is not a relationship health metric in CMDB Health. The Completeness KPI applies to CI data (Required and Recommended fields), not to relationships.
Expired relationships is not a recognized relationship health metric. The correct relationship metrics are Duplicate, Orphan, and Stale relationships.

source.excerpt: Measures the health of CI relationships, consisting of the following metrics which are not-configurable: Duplicate relationships... Orphan relationships - A relationship that is missing either a parent CI, a child CI, or both. Stale relationships - A relationship in which the parent CI or the child CI is a stale CI.

questions.question: Which business rule is responsible for synchronizing group attributes from a technical service offering to the underlying CIs part of a dynamic CI group?

options.text: Sync Ops Status for CMDB CI
CSDM Data Sync on TSO deletion
Sync teams to CI assigned groups
CSDM - Sync Group Attributes
CSDM Data Sync on Reclassification

CSDM Data Sync on TSO deletion handles cleanup when a TSO is deleted, not group synchronization.
Sync teams to CI assigned groups is not the correct business rule name for this functionality.
CSDM Data Sync on Reclassification handles CI reclassification scenarios, not group attribute synchronization.

questions.question: Which components are displayed on the CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboards?

Configuration Items, Relationships, and Business Services
Knowledge Articles, Service Catalog Items, and Catalog Categories
Foundational Metric Results, Priorities, and Remediation Playbook URLs

While CIs and relationships are measured by the dashboard, they are not the displayed components - metrics about them are.

options.text: From the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard, select and open the Duplicate Locations tile and then select Show Records
From the Locations table, configure an encoded query to search for duplicate records
From CMDB Workspace, configure a certification policy
From Query Builder, create a query to search for duplicate records

questions.question: Duplicate locations found in the location table can be caused by which configurations?

options.text: Naming standard for Locations has not been defined and/or published
A well thought out naming convention for location names has been defined and adopted
Source of location data is not maintained and has duplicates
Well tested import process for location names

explanation.correct: Duplicate locations are commonly caused by: (1) No defined/published naming standard for Locations, and (2) Source location data that is not maintained and contains duplicates. These upstream issues propagate duplicates into ServiceNow.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A well-defined naming convention prevents duplicates, it doesn't cause them.
A well-tested import process would catch and prevent duplicates, not cause them.

questions.question: What are the three pillars for successful foundational data in a ServiceNow CMDB?

Completeness
Correctness
Compliance
Insight
Ingest

wrongAnswers.explanation: Completeness is one of the three C's from the CMDB Health Dashboard, not the Data Foundations pillars.
Correctness is one of the three C's from the CMDB Health Dashboard, not the Data Foundations pillars.
Compliance is one of the three C's from the CMDB Health Dashboard, not the Data Foundations pillars.

questions.question: When configuring technical services, technical service offerings, and dynamic CI groups, which represents the relationships between each of them?

options.text: Technical service offering is the parent to a technical service
Technical service is the parent to a technical service offering
Technical service offering contains a Dynamic CI group
Dynamic CI group contains a technical service offering

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is reversed - Technical service is the parent, not the TSO.

Upstream Causes
Downstream Consequences
Remediation Plays

questions.question: From the Get Well Playbook "Percentage of Dynamic CI Groups with CMDB Group", which is a potential benefit to the business if this metric is properly governed?

Complicates the auto-population of affected CIs during changes
Reduces IT asset management tracking capabilities

Proper CI grouping enhances, not reduces, IT asset management capabilities.

questions.question: From the Get Well Playbook "Handle Duplicate CIs in your CMDB", what are potential benefits to the business if this metric is properly governed?

Decreases the speed of incident resolution and increases MTTR
Worsens accuracy in CI matching for Vulnerability Response
Reduces confusion from duplicate records appearing in the list view

wrongAnswers.explanation: Removing duplicates increases speed and decreases MTTR, not the opposite.
Removing duplicates improves accuracy in CI matching, not worsens it.

ServiceNow Community

questions.question: From the Get Well Playbook "Percent of Incidents referencing a CI", what are suggested solutions to ensure the configuration item field is populated on an incident form?

options.text: Configure field with reference qualifier to make it easier to find affected CI
Make the Configuration item field mandatory on the incident form once an incident state moves from In progress to Resolved
Configure scheduled job to run nightly to populate the field
Configure business rule to auto-populate the field

No review process in creation of CI classes
Highly skilled ServiceNow developers

questions.question: From the Get Well Playbook "Technical Service Offerings with Support Group or Change Group Populated", which is a potential benefit to the business if this metric is properly governed?

Simplicity in identifying owners and support groups for configuration items
Reduced accuracy in business decision-making
Complex reporting process for security incidents

wrongAnswers.explanation: Proper TSO configuration increases efficiency, not decreases it.
Better group data improves decision-making accuracy, not reduces it.
Having proper groups simplifies reporting, not complicates it.

Managed by Group

questions.question: Assuming business drivers are equal, from the CMDB Data Foundations Dashboard, the "Hardware CIs with Serial Numbers" Result displays 55% with a Priority of "3 - Medium-High", and the "CIs with Relationships to Parent and Child" the Result displays 20% with a Priority of "4- Medium". Which metric should action be taken on first?

options.text: Hardware CIs with Serial Numbers because serial numbers are key to asset health
Hardware CIs with Serial Numbers because Priority is more important than Result, in determining which metric to take action on first
Both Result and Priority are equally important
CIs with Relationships to Parent and Child because Result is more important than Priority, in determining which metric to take action on first

wrongAnswers.explanation: While serial numbers are important, priority ranking determines remediation order.
Result and Priority are not equally important - Priority takes precedence.
Result percentage alone doesn't determine priority - the Priority field does.

Run the fix script using a UI action
